TextBlock.Text: WESTERN APPROACH. The coalition's escort corridor runs on fuel that arrives from outside it, and the replenishment group coming up from the Indian Ocean is the reason anything in the Banda still has range.

The escort is a European rotation: a Type 45 with its Merlin, a German F124, a Dutch Karel Doorman, a Danish Iver Huitfeldt, an Italian FREMM and an older Type 23 that was already in the region when the crisis began. Two RAF Typhoons out of Curtin hold the air, with a Swedish AEW aircraft lent for the transit.

The Russian expeditionary detachment supporting the Biak enclave has put a MiG-35 pair and a Su-24MP up along the northern edge. They are here to find the tankers, and one of the MiGs carries an anti-ship missile. Take them down before they do.

AIR PICTURE / ARGUS 70: The Swedish GlobalEye reports a MiG-35 pair and a Su-24MP along the northern edge of the corridor. The force assesses one MiG as an anti-ship threat. Use the AEW picture to cue the Typhoons and ship sensors; keep both tankers covered while confirming the approaching tracks.
Captain (N) Elin Vasse, European escort rotation

The two tankers are the group. Everything east of here plans around what is in their tanks. The Russian shadowers to the north are hunting for the tankers; do not let them get close enough to find them.
• The replenishment group reaches the eastern box
• Splash the shadowers before they find the tankers

Two tankers. Type 45, F124, Karel Doorman, Iver Huitfeldt, FREMM, Type 23, Merlin, Wildcat, a Sea Lynx and an NH90 across the group. Two Typhoons and a Saab AEW&C overhead. Opposing: MiG-35 pair and a Su-24MP.
Complete the assigned task within 85 minutes. Command will close the operation at that deadline and the main task will be recorded as failed.
